questions.question: In the context of a linear layer in a neural network written as y = W x + b with x and y as column vectors, what is the interpretation of W as a linear map?
questions.choice_A: W maps input feature vectors to output activations by linearly combining input dimensions
questions.choice_B: W maps output activations back to input features via an inverse transformation
questions.choice_C: W only permutes the coordinates of x without scaling them
questions.choice_D: W applies a nonlinear transformation to x before linear combination

questions.question: Which statement about the transpose operation is most relevant for understanding gradients in linear layers?
questions.choice_A: Transpose preserves eigenvalues of any square matrix
questions.choice_B: The transpose converts a linear map from input-to-output space into a map that aligns with backpropagated gradients
questions.choice_C: Taking the transpose of W leaves its column space unchanged
questions.choice_D: The transpose is only defined for symmetric matrices

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Frobenius norm of a matrix W?
questions.choice_A: It is the largest absolute value among the eigenvalues of W
questions.choice_B: It is the square root of the largest eigenvalue of W^T W
questions.choice_C: It is the square root of the sum of the squares of all entries of W
questions.choice_D: It is the sum of the absolute values of all entries of W

questions.question: What does it mean for two vectors u and v in $\mathbb{R}^n$ to be orthogonal with respect to the standard inner product?
questions.choice_A: They have the same length
questions.choice_B: They are linearly dependent
questions.choice_C: Their entries sum to zero
questions.choice_D: Their inner product $u^\top v$ equals zero

questions.question: Which statement about the trace function is correct and useful in machine learning derivations?
questions.choice_A: The trace is invariant under cyclic permutations: $\operatorname{tr}(ABC) = \operatorname{tr}(BCA)$ when products are defined
questions.choice_B: The trace equals the product of the eigenvalues of a matrix
questions.choice_C: The trace is only defined for diagonal matrices
questions.choice_D: The trace is always equal to the matrix rank

questions.question: In the SVD $W = U \Sigma V^\top$, what do the columns of V represent in terms of the action of W?
questions.choice_A: Output-space orthonormal basis aligned with W's columns
questions.choice_B: Input-space orthonormal directions that W scales by singular values
questions.choice_C: Left eigenvectors associated with W's eigenvalues
questions.choice_D: An arbitrary basis with no geometric meaning

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the spectral (operator) norm $\|W\|_2$?
questions.choice_A: It equals $\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(W^\top W)}$
questions.choice_B: It equals the sum of singular values of W
questions.choice_C: It equals the largest singular value of W
questions.choice_D: It equals the largest absolute row sum of W

questions.question: For a real symmetric matrix $S$, which property is guaranteed and crucial for many learning algorithms?
questions.choice_A: S is always rank-1
questions.choice_B: S has complex eigenvalues in conjugate pairs
questions.choice_C: S is not diagonalizable
questions.choice_D: S has an orthonormal eigenbasis and is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix

questions.question: What does the rank of a weight matrix W in a linear layer indicate about its representational capacity?
questions.choice_A: The number of independent directions in input space that are preserved by W
questions.choice_B: The number of zero singular values
questions.choice_C: The total number of nonzero entries in W
questions.choice_D: The number of columns of W regardless of redundancy

questions.question: Which relationship between norms is correct and relevant for Lipschitz properties of neural layers?
questions.choice_A: $\|W\|_F \le \|W\|_2$ for all W
questions.choice_B: $\|Wx\|_2 \le \|W\|_2 \cdot \|x\|_2$ for all x
questions.choice_C: $\|W\|_2 = \|W\|_F$ if and only if W is square
questions.choice_D: $\|W\|_2$ equals the maximum absolute row sum

questions.question: Which statement about orthonormal bases is most accurate in the context of SVD?
questions.choice_A: Columns of U and V in the SVD form orthonormal bases for the row and column spaces respectively
questions.choice_B: Columns of U form an orthonormal basis for the nullspace of W
questions.choice_C: Columns of U and V form orthonormal bases for the column space of W and the row space of W respectively
questions.choice_D: Columns of V form an orthonormal basis for the column space of W

questions.question: If $W$ has SVD $W = U \Sigma V^\top$, which statement connects SVD to principal directions of the map?
questions.choice_A: Applying W to $v_i$ yields $\sigma_i u_i$, revealing how W scales the direction $u_i$
questions.choice_B: Applying W to $u_i$ yields $\sigma_i v_i$, revealing how W scales the direction $v_i$
questions.choice_C: Applying $W^\top$ to $u_i$ yields $\sigma_i v_i$, demonstrating the mapping from output to input principal directions
questions.choice_D: Applying $W^\top$ to $v_i$ yields $\sigma_i u_i$, demonstrating the mapping from input to output principal directions

questions.question: Which statement correctly relates the trace and eigenvalues of a square matrix $A$?
questions.choice_A: The trace equals the sum of eigenvalues (counting algebraic multiplicities)
questions.choice_B: The trace equals the product of eigenvalues
questions.choice_C: The trace equals the number of nonzero eigenvalues
questions.choice_D: The trace is independent of the eigenvalues

questions.question: Which description best matches the interpretation of neurons as column vectors of a weight matrix W in a fully connected layer?
questions.choice_A: Each column of W contains outgoing weights from an output neuron to all inputs
questions.choice_B: Each column of W represents the incoming weights feeding into a particular input feature
questions.choice_C: Each column of W represents the weights projecting a single input feature into all output neurons, i.e., a basis vector in output space scaled by that feature
questions.choice_D: Each column of W is the gradient of the loss with respect to an input neuron

questions.question: What is the nullspace (kernel) of a matrix W and why is it relevant for linear layers?
questions.choice_A: The set of all vectors mapped to zero by W; inputs in the nullspace produce zero pre-activations
questions.choice_B: The set of all outputs achievable by W; it characterizes expressivity
questions.choice_C: The set of left singular vectors of W; it indicates stability
questions.choice_D: The set of eigenvectors corresponding to the largest eigenvalue; it indicates dominance

questions.question: Which matrix is diagonalizable over the reals with an orthonormal eigenbasis?
questions.choice_A: Any real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix
questions.choice_B: Any real matrix with distinct singular values
questions.choice_C: Any diagonal matrix with nonzero entries
questions.choice_D: Any upper-triangular matrix

questions.question: Which statement correctly connects SVD and low-rank approximation for model compression?
questions.choice_A: Truncating small eigenvalues of $W^\top W$ produces the best rank-k approximation in spectral norm
questions.choice_B: Truncating to the top k singular values and corresponding singular vectors minimizes the approximation error in Frobenius norm
questions.choice_C: Zeroing arbitrary entries to achieve rank k yields the optimal low-rank approximation
questions.choice_D: SVD cannot be used for low-rank approximations of rectangular matrices

questions.question: Which relationship between SVD and the spectral norm is most useful for bounding layer sensitivity?
questions.choice_A: The spectral norm equals the smallest singular value
questions.choice_B: The spectral norm equals the Euclidean norm of the first column of U
questions.choice_C: The spectral norm equals the largest singular value, which upper-bounds $\|Wx\|_2/\|x\|_2$
questions.choice_D: The spectral norm equals the sum of the squares of all singular values

questions.question: Which statement about rank, column space, and row space is correct?
questions.choice_A: The rank equals the dimension of both the column space and the row space
questions.choice_B: The rank equals the number of zero columns
questions.choice_C: The row space and column space always have different dimensions for rectangular matrices
questions.choice_D: The rank equals the number of linearly independent rows minus the number of columns

questions.question: Which property differentiates the Frobenius norm from the spectral norm in terms of data sensitivity?
questions.choice_A: The Frobenius norm controls worst-case amplification of inputs
questions.choice_B: The spectral norm equals the square root of the sum of squared entries
questions.choice_C: The Frobenius norm aggregates energy across all directions, while the spectral norm captures the maximum amplification along a single direction
questions.choice_D: Both norms are identical for all matrices

questions.question: For a square matrix A with a complete set of linearly independent eigenvectors, which statement holds?
questions.choice_A: A is diagonalizable as $A = PDP^{-1}$ for some diagonal D
questions.choice_B: A must be symmetric
questions.choice_C: A must have distinct eigenvalues
questions.choice_D: A cannot be defective
